item.title: Government-chartered flight from Oman arrives in Dublin
item.description: A government chartered bringing Irish citizens out of the Middle East has touched down at Dublin Airport this morning. The aircraft left Muscat in Oman yesterday afternoon and arrived shortly before five am, after a delay during a stopover in Cairo, with 200 people on board. Foreign Affairs Minister Helen McEntee says 15 hundred people have returned on commercial flights in recent days, and is urging Irish citizens in the Middle East to register their presence. item.title: Local MEP welcomes EU commitment to combat period poverty
item.description: A local MEP says more work is needed to end menstrual poverty. It follows the EU's commitment to tackle period and menopause poverty, by exchanging best practices between Member States to inform new policies which will make period products more accessible and affordable. A 2018 report found that up to 85,000 women in Ireland are at risk of period poverty, with 50 per cent of girls aged 12-19 experiencing challenges accessing products due to cost, stigma, or lack of education. item.description: Passengers hoping to travel on the Galway to Dublin and Westport to Dublin rail lines are being reminded about disruption to services this weekend. item.title: Volunteers sought in Roscommon for over 50s mentoring service
item.description: Age and Opportunity are looking for volunteers in Roscommon for a mentoring service for the over 50s. item.title: Leitrim fall to Carlow in ladies league
item.description: Leitrim fell to their first defeat of the season falling to Carlow in Carrick-on-Shannon. Carlow maintained their perfect run in Division 4 of the Lidl National Football League when they chalked up their seventh win of the campaign. Carlow trailed, seven points to one at the break but then took over after the restart, running out 2-7 to 0-11 winners.
